<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 45 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dabe771824a273108ea219105ff9744e0f1e87c6` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0515b03654716cfc06332c4822e97a0714c1c0fe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts + .changeset/26775-manager-chain-depth.md (the prose face, read for ②), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts (`managerDeps` and the manager pass at its `applyUserManagerLink` call), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts (`linkDeps`, `linkDemoStaffManagers`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`find`: alias fold, `context` taken off the query, `fillQueryAstDefaults` fills no `limit`; `$in` as the engine's own batch-read spelling), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts (`managerOf` and its `sys_member` screen), docs/adr/0057-erp-authorization-core-business-units-and-scope-depth.md (D3 and the open/paid seam note), scripts/check-where-matcher-conformance.mjs and scripts/check-objectql-double-limit.mjs (the contract the two edited doubles are held to), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user-set-manager-action.test.ts (names the derivation but drives the CEL engine, not an engine double, so the new read cannot reach it).

Inputs: card #26775 (body and all three comments, the os-dev-report 6451194257 included), PR #26868 (body, file list, `git diff origin/main...pr-26868` at merge-base `0ea90c7a18`, 4 files, +267 / -7), and the check-runs on the head. Not the dispatch order and not the dispatching seat's conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Accept-set narrowing at `applyUserManagerLink`** (served to all three callers: `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager`, the import's manager pass, `linkDemoStaffManagers`). A link whose whole chain — the links above the proposed manager counted from the new edge (`walkChain`, `links` starts at 1) plus the longest chain of existing reports below the edited user (`deepestSubordinateChain`) — exceeds 20 is now refused `400 VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `details.reason: 'max_depth_exceeded'`; on `main` only the upper half was counted and the same link answered 200 and was written. **Right.** The arithmetic is `budget = MAX_MANAGER_CHAIN_DEPTH - walk.links` with refusal the moment `depth` exceeds `budget`, so a link is admitted exactly when `links + depth` is at most 20; traced at the boundary in ④.
2. **A clear never walks down.** `managerId: null` skips the whole block (`if (managerId !== null)`), so a clear cannot be refused for depth. **Right** — a clear cannot lengthen any chain.
3. **Refusal order unchanged.** self-assignment, manager-not-found, cross-organization, cycle / existing_loop, then depth; the downward walk runs only once the upward walk answered `ok`, and an upward `too_deep` short-circuits it. A cycle is still answered `409 cycle`, never `max_depth_exceeded`. **Right.**
4. **Refusal message text changed** to name the lower half. Not a contract: no consumer parses it, the tests pin status + code + `details.reason`, and `check:doc-authoring` (no tracker number in a runtime string) is green in Lint & Repo Gates. **Right.**
5. **Public surface: none moves.** `SUBORDINATE_READ_CHUNK` and `deepestSubordinateChain` are module-private; `MAX_MANAGER_CHAIN_DEPTH` stays 20; `SetUserManagerResult`, newly imported by the test, was already exported on `main`; no key of any schema moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. **Right.**
6. **Read shape of the new walk.** `sys_user where manager_id IN (level ids)`, `fields: ['id']`, `context: SYSTEM_READ_CTX` carried inside the query — the shape `findUser` has carried since the endpoint landed, and `ObjectQL.find` takes `context` off the query (`mergeReadContext(query?.context, options?.context)`). `$in` is the engine's own batch-read spelling (`engine-master-detail-related.ts`, `engine-referential-integrity.ts`). The read carries no `limit`, and the engine fills none (`fillQueryAstDefaults`: "`where`/`fields`/`limit`/`offset`/`top` carry no `.default()`"; no driver-side row cap found in `driver-sql` or `driver-memory`). That is the correct shape here, not an omission: a bound on a level read would truncate the level and under-count the chain — the silent-truncation class `check-objectql-double-limit` exists for, pointed at an authorization input. **Right.**
7. **Test doubles.** Both `matchesWhere` doubles now admit `$in` alone (one operator key, array payload) and keep throwing on every other operator object and on the combinators, which is the `check-where-matcher-conformance` criterion (answer correctly or refuse loudly, never silently wrong); both still apply `limit` by presence (`check-objectql-double-limit`). Both gates are green in Lint & Repo Gates. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: `patch`. **Right.** `Metadata-protocol: none`, so the level follows the kind alone: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one marker (`adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) with its reason (no key, export or type moves; the refusal is the existing envelope, so nothing for a migration to rewrite and no tombstone), the before / now / unchanged / who-sees-it / remedy prose, and both line-initial declarations. The PR title carries `!`; PR body and changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `(narrowing)` is the arm the diff publishes — an accept-set shrinks at a shipped endpoint and nothing widens. `Check Changeset`, `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:adr-0087-registration` are green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

From the os-dev-report (card comment 6451194257) and the PR body, each answered:

- **File surface widened to `admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts`**, outside the claim's named files. Answered: necessary, not scope creep. The import's manager pass calls `applyUserManagerLink` (`admin-import-users.ts:975`; `managerDeps.getDataEngine` returns the import's own engine), so the new `$in` read reaches that suite's double, which threw on every operator object. The edit is the minimal one (admit `$in` alone, keep refusing the rest) and the suite's own assertions are untouched. Accepted.
- **Commit trailers** use the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes, not the harness reminder's model-bearing one. Verified on both commits of `origin/main..pr-26868` (`Co-authored-by: Claude`, `Claude-Session:`). Accepted.
- **PR footer in the session-URL form**: the form AGENTS.md names for PR bodies. Accepted.
- **Gate derivation tree one commit behind `origin/main`, no merge of `main` made.** `main` has moved further since (`origin/main` `5787df4d4b` at review time, merge-base `0ea90c7a18`); no conflict reported, and the queue rebuilds the merge group. Not a finding.
- `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []` — nothing to escalate.
- **Card wording "the existing `too_deep` reason"**: the wire discriminator is `max_depth_exceeded` (`too_deep` is the walk-internal kind). The PR's acceptance note says so and the tests pin the wire value. Resolved; no escalation.
- **Premise**: the os-dev-report re-checked `let links = 1;` on `origin/main` `0ea90c7a18`; the pre-image hunk in the diff shows the upward-only walk at that line. Holds.
- **Check-runs on the head** (their conclusions are the gate verdicts; read at the moment this record was rendered): `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger all success), `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Check Changeset` success, `Check PR Size` success, `PR-body guards` success, `Test UI` success and `Dogfood Regression Gate` success (their path-filtered shards skipped: no `ui/` or dogfood path in the diff), `Lint UI` / `Type Check UI` / `Build & E2E UI` skipped by path filter; `Test Core` 1 of 8 shards concluded success, the other 7 still `in_progress` with no conclusion — an in-progress run is not a pass, so this record carries no verdict for those shards, and the owning seat reads them green before any landing act. No check on the head has concluded failure.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree at the head, not on the PR body's account of it.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.ts` — holds.**

- *Off-by-one at exactly 20, both orders and a middle join*, traced against `walkChain` and `deepestSubordinateChain`. Top-down: the k-th write (n_k reporting to n_(k-1)) sees `links = k` (1 for the edge plus k-1 ancestors) and no reports below, so k = 20 is admitted and k = 21 is refused by the upward walk's own past-20 check on `links` before any downward read. Bottom-up: the write of n_j reporting to n_(j-1) sees `links = 1` (n_(j-1) is still loose) and `depth = 21 - j` below, total `22 - j`: j = 2 gives 20 (admitted), j = 1 gives 21 (refused, not written). Middle join n10 reporting to n9 over a 9-link upper chain: `links = 10`, `budget = 10`; a lower chain of 11 answers `depth = 11`, refused; of 10 answers `depth = 10`, admitted at exactly 20. The edge case `links = 20` gives `budget = 0`: a user with any report is refused (total 21) and a leaf is admitted after one empty read. Correct in every case.
- *A cycle through the edited user or the proposed manager.* `walkChain` (unchanged, `seen`-guarded) runs first: a proposed manager that sits inside the edited user's own subtree has a `manager_id` chain that reaches `userId` and is answered `cycle`; an upstream loop is `existing_loop`; both return before the downward walk. Below the edited user, a `manager_id` loop can enter the BFS frontier only through the edited user itself (every node has one `manager_id`, so a loop not through `userId` is never reached), and that case is closed by seeding `seen` with `userId`. The walk terminates in every case.
- *Tenant / organization scoping versus the existing upward walk.* `sys_user` carries no `organization_id` (a global identity table — this file's refusal-4 note and `team-graph.ts` both say so), so there is nothing to scope the read by; the downward read uses the same `SYSTEM_READ_CTX` and the same no-org-predicate shape as the existing `findUser` upward walk and as `managerOf`. Counting a cross-organization report that the org-scoped rollup (ADR-0057 D3, "bounded ... and org-scoped") would screen out can only make the cap stricter than the rollup's walk, never looser — the right direction for a cap whose purpose is to bound that walk.
- *Cost bound under a wide tree.* One `$in` read per level per 500-id chunk, at most `budget + 1` levels (at most 21) however deep the subtree is, rows bounded by the subtree, a `seen` Set of subtree size in memory, no per-user read. The 500 chunk keeps every IN list under SQLite's historical parameter ceiling. Acceptable for a platform-admin write; the import's per-row link adds one empty level read per fresh user. The absence of a `limit` on the level read is deliberate and correct (①.6).
- *Can a refusal leave a partial write?* No. The single `engine.update` sits after every refusal and each refusal returns before it; the downward walk is read-only. Serialising concurrent links is not a property this design claims on `main` either and is outside the card.
- *Empty `$in`*: unreachable — the loop runs only while `level.length` is positive and each chunk is a non-empty slice.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.test.ts` — holds.** The new block pins the card's three asks at `runSetUserManager` with the HTTP envelope: TOP-DOWN and BOTTOM-UP over 21 edges (the first 20 answer 200, the 21st is refused on status + `error.code` + `details.reason`, the refused edge is unwritten, and `longestChain` of the table reads 20 from the rows, not from the handler); MIDDLE 9 + 1 + 11 refused and 9 + 1 + 10 admitted; the longest branch deciding over 30 shallow reports; the level-read shape (exactly 20 reads for budget 19, the second read naming all 40 heads in one `$in`, pinned on the arguments the engine received); and the loop-through-the-edited-user termination. `engine.updates` is asserted on every refusal.
- **should-fix (comment only):** in "the subordinate walk reads one level per query…", the comment says "40 direct reports, each with a chain of MAX - 1 below it: 1 + MAX links", but the loop builds `MAX_MANAGER_CHAIN_DEPTH + 5` nodes per branch, 25 links below `x`. The assertion (exactly 20 level reads, nothing read past the proven crossing) holds for any branch deeper than 20 and is the stronger pin; only the prose misstates the fixture. Correct the comment when the file is next touched.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users-manager-pass.test.ts` — holds.** The same `$in`-only admission as the sibling double; combinator and other-operator refusals untouched; `limit` still applied. The import's manager-pass assertions are unchanged, which is right: the import gains the refusal through the shared derivation and its reporting does not move (`noteManagerFailure(r, refusal.reason, refusal.message)` passes the reason through unchanged).

*Cited code, read to judge the above, not reviewed:* `demo-staff.ts` `linkDemoStaffManagers` hands the provisioning engine straight to the link (`linkDeps.getDataEngine`), so a `demoStaff` chain past 20 is refused on the boot with the refusal text in `outcome.failed`, and a chain of at most 20 links passes in any declaration order; `admin-import-users.ts` catches a throw from the link per row and reports it as `unresolved` without failing the import, which bounds the blast radius should an engine ever refuse the `$in` shape. The refusal-3 docblock's cite — "the reference resolver in `packages/qa/dogfood` bounds itself at 20 levels" — resolves: `showcase-scope-depth.dogfood.test.ts` (and its fallback sibling) register an `IHierarchyScopeResolver` whose `own_and_reports` arm walks `sys_user where manager_id IN (frontier)`, `fields: ['id']`, system context, a `seen` set, for `d` below 20 — the same read shape and the same bound `deepestSubordinateChain` now enforces at the write, so a chain this endpoint admits is one that resolver walks in full. ADR-0057 D3's "bounded (hard cap + cache, mirroring the `org_user_ids` cap) and org-scoped" is the contract the cap serves, and the open/paid seam note places the production resolver in `@objectstack/security-enterprise`, outside this tree — nothing downstream in this repo would catch the chain this PR now refuses, which is why the write-time enforcement is the right place.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 1 should-fix (test-comment accuracy).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-26775-manager-chain-depth`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYmQXM3rHJcPnrEPk4B`

**VERDICT: PASS**
